# Regression with Interaction

> Learning Objectives
>
> 1. Understand interaction effects in regression models
> 2. Distinguish between main effects and interaction effects
> 3. Interpret regression coefficients in an interaction model
> 4. Compute and interpret simple slopes


## Introduction

**Main Effects vs Interaction Effects**

In a main-effects regression model, each predictor affects the response independently.

For example, suppose we want to predict weight using sex and height:

$$
\text{Weight} = \beta_0 + \beta_s \text{SEX} + \beta_h \text{HEIGHT}
$$

Here:

+ $\beta_s$ represents the effect of sex
+ $\beta_h$ represents the effect of height

In this model, the effect of height is assumed to be the same for males and females.

However, this assumption may not be realistic. It is possible that height affects weight differently for males and females.

To allow the relationship to vary, we add an interaction term.

Interaction Model

The regression model with interaction becomes

$$
\text{Weight} =
\beta_0
+
\beta_s \text{SEX}
+
\beta_h \text{HEIGHT}
+
\beta_{sh} (\text{SEX} \times \text{HEIGHT})
$$

Important interpretation rule:

::: {.callout-note title="Warning: Important"}

When an interaction is included, the coefficients of the individual variables are no longer overall main effects.

Instead, they represent the effect when the interacting variable equals 0.

:::

Interpreting the Interaction Model

Assume

+ SEX = 0 for males
+ SEX = 1 for females

Model for males

Substitute $SEX = 0$

$$
\text{Weight}_{male} =
\beta_0 + \beta_h \text{HEIGHT}
$$

Model for females

Substitute $SEX = 1$

$$
\text{Weight}_{female} =
\beta_0 + \beta_s + (\beta_h + \beta{sh}) \text{HEIGHT}
$$

Interpretation:

+ Male slope = $\beta_h$
+ Female slope = $\beta_h + \beta_{sh}$

Thus,

$$
\beta_{sh}
$$

measures how the slope changes between males and females.
